races.name: AJA Novice Flat Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes (For Riders With 3 Wins Or Fewer At Start Of Season)

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with strong Good-ground form who finished 1st and 2nd in his last two starts on similar going at 8f; Liam Baxter takes the ride and his prominent style makes him ideally placed to exploit a controlled pace from Hatamoto.
runners_data.comment: Sandret has winning form in his recent starts — a winner four starts back and a second five starts back — but back-to-back eighths in his last two outings are a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and arrives fit enough on 31 days' rest carrying 159 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has hit the frame five times in his last seven starts at 8f on Good, with Jack Lander's trainer returning 1/3 over 14 days; his tendency to press the pace makes him a natural second wheel to Hatamoto here.
runners_data.comment: Tees George has been a model of consistency without a win, posting two placings in his last six starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 156 lb burden is the chief concern for a gelding rated just 59.

runners_data.name: Deep Sleep
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who consistently finishes in the first four on Good ground (7/7 sim-going record) but is rated 64 and carries 155lbs; usually prominent but has been reluctant to fully commit in headgear, dropping as far back as 12th on a softer surface previously.
runners_data.comment: Deep Sleep has shown consistent placing ability with three fourths in his last five starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 155 lb from stall nine is the concern for a gelding yet to score, though he shapes as a serious threat here.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse on a seven-race losing streak who has failed to place on similar going and carries a light 154lbs; nothing in the recent form suggests a reversal here and a 1m flat track is not obviously in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Tropez Power has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating gives him a slim but genuine edge on this card, but he arrives winless in his last five starts and must show more than a run of mid-to-rear finishes suggests he currently can.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner with two recent wins at 8f on Good — this is his optimal scenario; Miss Burley is trusted to cross and lead from gate, and on these terms he will be very hard to peg back before the distance.
runners_data.comment: Hatamoto ran a fine second last time out and has winning form in his last six starts, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour at draw one carrying 153 lb — the chief concern is a trainer currently among the most out-of-form in recent weeks.

runners_data.name: Calaxy
runners_data.note: 198-day absence rings alarm bells; all recent form was on Standard or Heavy surfaces where he struggles (2/10 in similar going), and the significant layoff for a four-year-old in a handicap with Mark Loughnane's yard returning 1/17 is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning from a 198-day absence, Calaxy faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a fourth three starts back suggests some ability worth noting.

runners_data.name: Jungle Knight
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old whose sole win came on Soft ground over 7f; his hold-up style means he needs gaps to appear in the straight, and his Good-ground figures (4/9) suggest he finds this surface less congenial than softer conditions.
runners_data.comment: Jungle Knight lands a win two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating putting him ahead of his official mark — the main concern is whether 57 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Suzette
runners_data.note: A genuine late-runner by nature who has been mapped to midfield given the overcrowded hold-up group — her true style means she'd prefer to come from further back, but on this flat track there may be too much to do from her likely race position; 0W1P on Good in 15 starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Suzette at least brings distance and going experience to the table, but an unplaced effort last time and a weight of 150 lb are negatives to weigh against a our rating of 61 that suggests she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Racing just four days after her last run, she brings strong placed form (five top-three finishes in last six) on Good ground; she's a natural hold-up horse placed into midfield by the crowded field shape, but her consistency makes her the most dangerous of the redistributed quartet if she finds daylight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Misemerald makes a quick reappearance just four days after her latest win, though that effort aside she has largely filled minor roles in recent starts, and 149 lb is a stiff burden to overcome at this level.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a patchy recent record, last winning 73 days ago over distances longer than today's mile; a true hold-up type who has been shuffled into midfield by the field's composition, and Good ground at 8f is not his optimum based on a 1W2P record in 15 attempts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Dandy's Angel faces a stiff task here, though a return to today's distance and going at least offers some familiarity after 73 days off.

runners_data.name: Harswell River
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a consistent placed record (0W4P) on Good ground over 8-10f and racing in cheekpieces; a hold-up racer shifted into midfield by the overcrowded back group, her best chance comes if she finds a clear passage from the two-furlong pole — a real traffic risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Harswell River faces a stiff task at 137 lb from stall 8, though a second three starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hatamoto is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good turf over one mile at Thirsk — a flat, straightforward track that rewards those who travel comfortably and sustain their effort. The pace will be moderate rather than scorching: Hatamoto has won twice from the front at this trip on similar ground and Miss Rebecca Burley is unlikely to be pressured into going faster than she needs to. Behind the leader, Sandret and Tees George should slot prominently, with Deep Sleep also wanting to race in the first half of the field, creating a reasonably ordered race shape rather than a chaotic scrimmage. This setup — a single unhurried front-runner, a small clutch of prominent racers sitting just off the pace, and a crowded hold-up group — classically favours horses racing prominently at a sustainable tempo, as they avoid traffic, save energy in the early stages and have first run on the hold-up horses entering the straight. The field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically get to the rear: Suzette, Misemerald, Dandy's Angel and Harswell River are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, with Hatamoto and, to a lesser degree, Sandret and Tees George most likely to secure their natural position and dictate the terms.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hatamoto controls, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto sets a comfortable lead and the pace stays honest without acceleration until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto bowls along in front unchallenged, Sandret and Tees George track in the slipstream and have first run entering the home straight; the hold-up horses face traffic and are too far back to close in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racer overpowers leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sandret, Tees George or Deep Sleep track Hatamoto throughout and produce more at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: One of the prominent trio sits a length off Hatamoto throughout, conserving energy while the leader does the donkey work, then kicks past inside the final furlong on Good ground that rewards sustained galloping.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse threads through
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to set up a proper finish and a hold-up runner finds a clear run.
scenarios.body: Misemerald, who has placed five times in her last five starts on similar Good ground and clearly goes well fresh enough after only 4 days, is the likeliest beneficiary if gaps appear; her consistent form figures (234231) suggest she stays on without needing a slow-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto crawls early and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A tight, dawdling pace would compress the field and allow any horse with a turn of foot to motor past, but most runners here are stayers or grinders rather than pure sprinters and the amateur jockey dynamic makes a true dawdle less likely.

watchPoints.text: Hatamoto's early lead is the race's pivot point — watch whether Miss Burley crosses quickly from her draw; if she is slow away or another horse presses her, the race shape changes entirely.

Misemerald runs just four days after her last race; watch her in the paddock and early strides for any sign the quick turnaround has taken its toll, as her form figures are otherwise the most consistent in the field.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Suzette, Misemerald, Dandy's Angel, Harswell River) will all be competing for the same late runs into the straight — watch for a bunching incident entering the home turn as they try to find their positions.

Calaxy has not run for 198 days and all her placed form is on artificial or heavy surfaces; watch for any market moves that might indicate stable confidence, otherwise treat the absence as a significant risk flag.

Deep Sleep's trainer returns 5/46 over 14 days — a cold yard angle — and his recent form shows a pattern of modest placings without conviction; watch whether his prominent style gets him into a challenging position or whether he weakens once headed.

races.name: Caddick Construction EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Ivegate Building Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer with solid recent form (three runs in the six-furlong band all finishing 2nd or 5th on good), handled well by Tudhope who is adept at threading through a big field; needs the honest pace set by County Carlow and Kats Bob to actually materialise into a gap at the furlong pole.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, Yes I'm Mali does offer some encouragement with two seconds in that sequence, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; however, a fifth last time out and 132 lb to carry are both against him here.

runners_data.name: Big Cyril
runners_data.note: Returns after 396 days off for Roger Fell, a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is modest at 1/12; Joanna Mason takes the ride and the horse has decent good-ground form over six furlongs but the huge absence from racing is the dominant concern here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for over a year, Big Cyril faces a stiff task here, with a finishing record of mostly mid-pack sixths doing little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a speed figure of 91 offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type whose recent form figures (7-0-0-8-0) tell a bleak story on good ground — sim-going record reads just 6 from 15 — and the horse has been out of the first six in every recent start on comparable terms; hard to make a case from the current data.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Eye Of Dubai nevertheless catches the eye on our rating of 98 — well clear of his official mark — and he returns fit on 13 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the worry is that his recent finishes offer little to cling to.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Wore headgear on a visor tag, handled by Oisin Orr for Ruth Carr who has been quietly active at 2/26 over 14 days; this horse's natural style is prominent, but with eight runners competing for that ground he is most likely to be crowded back and race in a position that blunts his chance — a top-six start would help considerably.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the majority of his rivals on our figures, Woodstock faces a stiff task from stall 15 carrying 131 lb, and while he won last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, he holds little appeal at this level.

runners_data.name: County Carlow
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners; Ben Haslam's three-year-old has shown the ability to lead at six furlongs and has form on similar going with a win at this trip in a softer event; Andrew Mullen will need to hold off Kats Bob's early challenge cleanly from the gates or risk burning the horse out before the straight.
runners_data.comment: County Carlow has a win and two runner-up finishes in recent starts, but he finished seventh last time out and ranks fifteenth of nineteen on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights off 130 lb from stall 18.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's six-year-old holds genuinely strong form on good ground (three placings from the last four) but is a true hold-up horse repositioned in midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed; Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) is positive, and the honest pace suits, but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's veteran front-runner is the second confirmed pace-setter and has finished 2nd twice at this trip on good ground recently; Jake Dickson (5lb claimer) is an unknown quantity at this level, and the horse's recent record includes two 20th-place finishes that flag inconsistency — will set the pace but may not finish it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Kats Bob faces a stiff task, though back-to-back second-place finishes two and three starts back show some ability, and he has experience over today's trip and going after a short 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced three-year-old arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and carries a top weight of 137lbs, but the 55-day absence is a small query; Ray Dawson has been working well with this yard, and the horse's natural prominent style suits the predicted race shape — gets a clean run from off County Carlow and this could be a straightforward bounce-back.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and rated well below his official rating, Anyasi is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last three starts, and 55 days off plus a high draw add further questions, though he has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: We Never Stop
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old prominently raced but is specifically flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — the worst combination in a truly-run race where the prominent position will be hotly contested and the gallop honest; the sim-going record of 8/15 is underwhelming, and Kevin Stott will struggle to find a winning angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, We Never Stop showed a flash of ability when second two starts back but has otherwise struggled for consistency, and a trainer firing at just 4% recently offers little confidence, though he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's ten-year-old is a genuine prominent racer with a recent win over six furlongs on good ground (1/6f/GOO in the last five runs), but this horse has been pushed into a midfield mapping because the prominent ground is saturated; Lauren Young (5lb) is worth a positive mention, though the style compromise reduces the winning chance relative to his ability.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Jordan Electrics arrives on a sharp seven-day turnaround carrying 136 lb from stall one, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; an eighth four starts back is the blot on an otherwise competitive profile.

runners_data.name: Starmade
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old has won twice at six furlongs on standard ground and PJ McDonald takes the ride with authority; the 50-day absence is manageable for a well-schooled horse, and the prominent style fits the predicted shape — one of the cleaner profiles in the field if he gets his natural spot behind the pace.
runners_data.comment: Starmade won two of his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, but has been unplaced last time out after 50 days off; he has run over today's trip and going before, and while our rating gives him claims, 134 lb from stall 17 may test him.

runners_data.name: Woven
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's veteran ten-year-old is a hold-up type with a recent 2nd at six furlongs on good ground, but the 53-day break and the horse's advanced age make sustained improvement unlikely; Connor Beasley knows the horse well but the sim-going record of 6/15 is not encouraging for a big-field sprint.
runners_data.comment: Woven shaped with clear promise when second two starts back, and his rating of 98 gives him a strong case as one of the chief dangers here; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 134 lb from stall seven, though the 53-day absence and a winless recent run of form are the main cautions.

runners_data.name: Art Lover
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends a three-year-old hold-up horse who finished 2nd twice over this course and distance combination (two 2nd-place finishes over 6f on good); Cieren Fallon is a smart booking and the headgear tag (t) suggests some freshening — needs the honest pace to set up a late run from off the speed and the talent is clearly there.
runners_data.comment: Art Lover showed well to finish second last time out, and a winner four starts back, but his two runs in between were disappointing; he has experience of today's distance and going, yet 48 days off and carrying 133 lb from stall nine give this a mixed look.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is one of the most experienced horses in the field with two wins over six furlongs on good ground in recent history; a genuine prominent type competing for limited space — David Allan is strong and may muscl the horse onto the early lead, which would be a net positive if the pace doesn't blow apart.
runners_data.comment: Manila Scouse has run over today's trip and going, and a winner three starts back gives him a form line to point to, but consecutive unplaced runs since and a trainer striking at just 5% in the last fortnight are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Topwarrior
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old carries top weight with headgear (tb — tongue-strap and blinkers) and has not won on good ground recently (sim-going 4/11, zero wins); a 62-day absence plus a hold-up style on a day the race pace will be contested makes this a difficult profile to get right.
runners_data.comment: Topwarrior showed his best when winning three starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going to call on; the main concern is returning from 62 days off having been unplaced on his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Deep Havana
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's five-year-old has placed four times in a row without winning — four 2nd-place finishes are prominent in the recent form — and returns from 135 days off; the limited going history (just two runs in the data) makes assessment speculative, but the prominent style is a fit if the jockey can navigate the large field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Deep Havana faces a stiff task here, and 135 days off the track adds another question mark; four runner-up finishes do at least suggest consistency, and he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Durham Castle
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's five-year-old has two wins over six furlongs on good ground in recent history and the sim-going record of 5/8 is solid; Callum Shepherd picks up a prominent runner returning from 74 days off, and this horse's profile — proven on this going and trip — sits near the top of the prominent-style pecking order in this field.
runners_data.comment: Durham Castle showed a smart turn of foot when winning three starts back, but back-to-back sixth and fifth placings since suggest he's found things tough, and a 74-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer striking at 30% offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old has an outstanding sim-going record of 12/15 with two wins and seven placings over six furlongs on good ground; Alex Jary (3lb) is a positive, and the horse races in the prominent style that this race shape directly rewards — consistent, proven, and well-placed if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Lord Roxby brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going before, but 140 lb is a stiff burden and his trainer has drawn a blank in 22 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has placed in five of the last six outings on good ground at six furlongs and is ridden by Conor Whiteley (5lb); the prominent style suits the predicted shape and the sim-going record of 8/12 is sound, though the lack of a recent win is a mild concern in a field that contains several proven winners.
runners_data.comment: Veblen Good arrives here in good nick off a 12-day turnaround, and his third three starts back and his victory six starts back underline a profile that our rating of 99 ranks narrowly top of this 19-runner field; the burden of 139 lb from stall 13 is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old has three wins from 13 good-ground runs and a recent 3rd at five furlongs; David Nolan is a strong rider and the prominent style is a natural fit — the return to six furlongs from five is a positive step given the horse's best form comes at this trip, and the honest pace suits a sustained finisher.
runners_data.comment: Novello Lad won twice in his last five starts but has been unplaced most recently, and 34 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 138 lb from stall 16 is no easy ask.

races.paceDynamic: County Carlow and Kats Bob are the confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the gates, creating a genuine, honest gallop on good ground over six furlongs — this is not a false-pace scenario. Eight of twenty runners want prominent ground, producing a congested early chase pack and real traffic danger from the two-furlong pole where runners will fan wide or become pocketed. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically occupy those positions, with Jordan Electrics, Manila Scouse and Woodstock the most likely to actually secure early cover given their gate habits and jockey experience, while others will be shuffled back involuntarily. With the gallop honest and the track flat, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit a length or two off a genuine pace and produce a clean, sustained finish — true prominent racers tracking in the first half-dozen who get a clean run at the two-furlong marker will be best placed, while genuine hold-up horses will need a clear split to benefit from the strong tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-And-Strike
scenarios.trigger: If County Carlow and Kats Bob force a genuine pace and a tracker settles just off them in the first five, poised for a clean two-furlong run.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop stretches the field and a prominent racer who is never further than third or fourth can exploit the pace collapse of the front two entering the final furlong; Thirsk's flat six favours a sustained, controlled surge rather than a late swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Stolen Victory
scenarios.trigger: If County Carlow or Kats Bob crosses quickly to the rail, dictates a controlled gallop faster than rivals expect, and the chasing pack is tardy in going for them.
scenarios.body: The lead horse gets the run of the race unchallenged and Thirsk's flat, galloping track means a well-rated front-runner with tactical pace can nick an uncontested lead before the big field organises; the weight of traffic congestion slows the main pack's response.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack over-races in the early scrum and the pace blows up sharply, leaving a gap on the outside for hold-up types to sprint through.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse sitting off the tempo by four or five lengths will find the final furlong yielding as the prominent runners stop in front; Thirsk's track does not exaggerate the closer's advantage, so this requires a genuine pace collapse, not just an honest gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the eight prominent runners bunch into a wall two furlongs out, causing interference that eliminates several fancied runners and a luckier midfield horse sneaks through.
scenarios.body: A horse redistribution scenario where a true prominent racer forced into midfield finds a gap when others check; the chaotic middle-race sequence produces an unexpected winner rather than the form book choice.

watchPoints.text: County Carlow and Kats Bob will clash at the head of affairs from the start — if neither yields cleanly, the early pace could burn both out before the two-furlong marker, fundamentally altering which runners can sustain a challenge.

With eight horses pressing for prominent positions, watch for traffic trouble between the two- and three-furlong markers as the field compresses on the flat track — horses on the inner rail are most exposed.

Jordan Electrics, Manila Scouse and Woodstock are true prominent types mapped into midfield — if any of these three over-commits early to reclaim their natural position, they risk burning out and creating gaps that can unseat others.

Big Cyril returns from 396 days off — if the horse is ring-rusty in a large, fast-moving field, Joanna Mason could find herself in difficulty in the early-race scramble, creating a danger to horses immediately behind.

Lord Roxby and Durham Castle both carry strong good-ground profiles and prominent styles — watch which of the two secures cleaner early cover, as that positioning detail is likely to separate them in the closing stages.

races.name: Frameclad Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Palmar Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent 7f performer on Good going with a sim-going record of 7/15 and a creditable 1W2P return; genuine hold-up racer who will look to close late, but with so many horses crowding the rear Ralph Beckett's five-year-old may find traffic a problem before getting a clear run.|
runners_data.comment: Palmar Bay shaped with real promise when third last time out, returns fit on 26 days' rest, and has run over today's trip and going before, giving his claims solid grounding; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Step up from six to seven furlongs for Tom Clover's four-year-old is a potential concern, as all five recent runs are over the minimum trip; Cieren Fallon takes the ride and the horse handles Good, but the trip extension makes this a question-mark start and its natural closing style will be compromised by the crowded rear group.|
runners_data.comment: Invictus Gold has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable 139 lb from stall 2, and our rating of 101 marks him out as a leading threat in this field — though he is winless in his last five starts, including an unplaced effort last time, and that inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, Connor Beasley will be able to bowl along unchallenged and set whatever tempo he chooses; his sim-going figure of 14/15 on Good is outstanding and he was last seen winning over this trip, making him a serious candidate to control and potentially steal the race — though at OR 97 he carries a weight burden and the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution that he is occasionally raced out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Northern Express shaped as the one to beat here, winning two starts back and recording a placed effort last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the 138 lb burden is the one query, but his rating of 105 marks him out as the class act in a field of 14.

runners_data.name: He's A Monster
runners_data.note: 369 days off the track is a significant flag for Hamad Al Jehani's six-year-old, and the hold-up style means he will need everything to fall right on first run back; handled Soft and Good alike in his form string but the layoff alone makes him a speculative participant rather than a banker.|
runners_data.comment: He's A Monster arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and conditions, with an official rating of 97; the one concern is that 369-day absence, which must be overcome fresh.

runners_data.name: Bobby Bennu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's five-year-old has headgear noted and a natural prominent style that fits this pace map well — with his best recent run a second at 7f he could sit just off Northern Express and deliver a sustained challenge; Ray Dawson rides and a sim-going mark of 9/15 is solid, though he is flagged as historically racing from hold-up position, so watching how he positions early will be key.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bobby Bennu does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two runs back hints at some ability; however, he has struggled for consistency and faces a stiff task from a mark of 94 carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David Tudhope's mount arrives on the back of a run just eight days ago and his form string shows a string of nines — a noted finisher who fades in the finish is a troubling tag for a seven-furlong race on Good ground; the prominent style may allow him to travel well before the final furlong, but his tendency to not see it out limits his winning claims.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mirsky arrives on a quick turnaround of eight days and has run over today's trip and going before, yet a sequence of three consecutive ninths is hard to overlook; carrying 133 lb from stall five, he looks a hard-to-fancy midfield proposition.

runners_data.name: Superposition
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald on Ed Dunlop's five-year-old who won over 7f Good and has placed at six furlongs too — a genuine each-way contender if the pace stacks up; his hold-up style is authentic and his 1W2P sim-going record of 6/15 is moderate, but recent form of 091349 shows he found a win not long ago and could outrun a price.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Superposition arrives here fit on a 30-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on, though a ninth last time out and carrying 132 lb from stall 6 are points against him.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Wilko
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old is genuinely a hold-up horse by nature, but with so many closers in this field his sim-going record of 5/15 and absence of a win in this going context is a concern; Kevin Stott rides and there is some 6f Tapeta form, but the STYLE_FIT flag and the redistribution mean he is unlikely to operate from his preferred position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 62 days off, Sergeant Wilko faces questions about fitness and consistency, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 93 offers some encouragement — a trainer in poor recent form (1/28) adds further concern.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Two wins from nine starts on Good going over 7f is an encouraging stat for Richard & Peter Fahey's five-year-old, and Warren Fentiman claims three pounds; the visor (hg:v) is noted as a headgear flag, but as a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by the race shape, the claim rider and the style mismatch compound the challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has disappointed in both runs since, leaving his recent form mixed; has run over today's trip and going, and 27 days off could mean he returns refreshed, though a mark of 85 and ranking tenth of fourteen suggest he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves on Roger Fell's six-year-old who sports a visor and an excellent sim-going strike rate of 11/15 — six consecutive placed or winning efforts on Good make this horse a consistent, prominent performer; recently won at 7f Good and the 212022 form string is full of placed efforts, suggesting he will be very competitive tracking the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Alpha Capture is hard to fancy against this field despite a tidy recent profile of three seconds in his last four completed starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight of 125 lb from stall 12 adds no help to his cause.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old runs just six days after its last outing and David Allan rides; a natural closer who is pushed into midfield by the pace dynamics, the short turnaround and a sim-going record of 10/15 with just one win at six furlongs on Soft suggest the step to seven on Good may stretch him.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Brighton Boy is hard to fancy despite a third last time out and experience over today's distance and going; a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the past fortnight adds little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's four-year-old wears a hood (hg:p) and has shown a placed effort at 8f Good in recent history; naturally a hold-up racer repositioned by the map, and with a STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 and no wins in Good going, M.P. Sheehy faces a stiff task against more exposed handicap performers.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Perfect Part does at least return quickly on eight days' rest and has experience of today's distance and going; a second four starts back offers some encouragement, though fifth last time out and a weight of 124 lb from stall 13 make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Majestic Dane
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old is lightly raced with just two career starts (12), both on Standard at 7f, so the switch to Good turf is entirely uncharted; won last time out and Clifford Lee rides, making this an interesting unknown — the age and experience gap against seasoned handicappers is the main risk.|
runners_data.comment: Majestic Dane shaped well enough in his last two starts, winning one and finishing second the other, and he has run over today's trip before, but a 190-day absence and a rating of 67 — ranking him last of 14 — make him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old has a headgear note (hg:h) and a strong sim-going record of 14/15, operating mainly at distances beyond today's trip — all recent form is at 8f to 10f, making seven furlongs a shorter test; Luke Morris rides and this is a genuine hold-up horse forced forward by map congestion, reducing its ability to deliver a late burst.|
runners_data.comment: Frankies Dream has been winless in his last six starts, finishing eighth in each of his past two outings, and ranked thirteenth of fourteen on our figures he faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip and going is genuinely in his favour, but little else encourages.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse inclined to lead in a 14-runner field, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being seriously pressured. Bobby Bennu, Mirsky, Alpha Capture and Majestic Dane are the likeliest prominent settlers, tracking a pace that is likely to be honest but not frenetic on Good ground over seven furlongs at Thirsk. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Sergeant Wilko, Our Havana, Perfect Part, Brighton Boy and Frankies Dream are all true closers who will be forced forward of their natural position, meaning they will not enjoy the late-race energy reserves their running style depends on. With one measured pace-setter and a clear highway for those sitting just off the front, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers with a proven ability to quicken from a stalking position — horses who can sit second or third, conserve energy in a controlled race, and deliver a sustained run from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express sets a calm, uncontested lead and prominent trackers conserve enough energy to pick him off in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Northern Express dictates from the front without being tested, allowing Bobby Bennu and Alpha Capture to travel comfortably in his slipstream before delivering their challenge; on Good ground at seven furlongs this is the classic Thirsk setup where horses who race prominently but not on the lead have a structural advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Northern Express Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely modest and Northern Express gets an unchallenged, slow-motion lead that allows him to conserve enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: With a small gap between his cruising speed and the field's chase-down pace, Northern Express could turn a seven-furlong race into a procession if the other prominent horses fail to apply pressure early enough; his excellent course-distance form and high sim-going score of 14/15 on Good underline the danger.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected through the first half and prominent horses are drawn into a burn-up, leaving late energy for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: In this scenario the forced redistribution is reversed — a runner like Superposition or Palmar Bay, racing nearer their true style, picks up the pieces as the pace collapses in front of them; Superposition's win at 7f on Good and Palmar Bay's consistent placed form at this trip make them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses push forward to dispute the lead, creating an unexpectedly strong gallop that breaks the race open for any survivor.
scenarios.body: This shape is unlikely given the clear pecking order, but if Bobby Bennu or Majestic Dane decides to press Northern Express hard from the outset the collapse of the front group could hand a scrambling chance to whichever runner avoids the melee; with several hold-up types miscast in midfield, a true late finisher winning from the back is improbable even in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Northern Express (Connor Beasley) gets a completely uncontested lead — if no other prominent horse moves to press him before halfway, the controlled pace could allow him to steal several lengths on the field turning for home.

Sergeant Wilko, Our Havana, Brighton Boy, Perfect Part and Frankies Dream are all natural hold-up horses who will be squeezed into midfield — watch for a bottleneck on the turn that could hamper multiple runners simultaneously.

Majestic Dane is entirely unexposed on Good turf and has only two career runs — any erratic or greenish behaviour from the three-year-old in a 14-runner field on a flat track could create interference for those racing close by.

Alpha Capture's visor and consistent placed form on Good ground make him one to monitor for early positioning — if he slots smoothly into second or third behind Northern Express he is likely to be involved at the business end.

He's A Monster returns from 369 days off — watch how he moves in the paddock and how quickly he settles; a rusty reappearance could see him drop away quickly and cause disruption in a tightly packed mid-pack.

races.name: Applebridge Group Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pinatique
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's operation runs this mare back quickly (13 days) which typically signals a readiness to perform; a genuine hold-up horse who needs cover and a strong pace to close into, and her best form has come at 10-12f suggesting 1m6f is an acid test of stamina.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pinatique at least returns on a quick 13-day turnaround in fair condition, and her fourth last time out offers a shade of encouragement, though a rating of 83 leaves her with ground to make up on the principals.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner with strong place-record at 1m6f-plus on good ground, wearing a hood; returning after 54 days and gets a clear lead if Talismans Time is outgunned early, which is when this horse is most dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Sax Appeal has been consistently placed, finishing third in three of his last four completed starts, and has run over today's distance and going before, giving him solid claims here; fifty-four days off is worth noting, though his profile makes him our preferred pick at 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's colt is a natural prominent racer with a win at 12f on good ground; stepping up in trip from recent runs but the Varian yard is in decent form (T14: 6/17) and this horse's cruising style suits a genuinely run staying test.
runners_data.comment: Sudu landed a win three starts back and returns after a 21-day break in good order, with experience of today's going working in his favour; the risk is that his last two outings have both been well below that winning level.

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who will push for the lead from the off; has a solid record in good-ground handicaps over 14-16f and Cian Horgan (5lb claim) reduces the weight burden, though taking on Sax Appeal for supremacy could leave both vulnerable.
runners_data.comment: Talismans Time shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here on a retrieval mission just 17 days later, having run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts and must bounce back from two below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Mick Collins
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong record over 16-20f in good-going handicaps including two wins; trainer has only one runner in a 14-day window suggesting limited current activity, but David Nolan takes over in the saddle which is a positive booking and this trip is firmly in his wheelhouse.
runners_data.comment: Mick Collins bolsters his claims with a win two starts back and goes on today's going, while our rating of 90 puts him clear at the head of this field; the concern is that seventh last time out leaves him needing to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Hamadhan
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has been off 90 days — the longest layoff in this field — which introduces significant fitness uncertainty; has placed on good ground but has consistently run over shorter distances than today's 1m6f, and the combination of a stiff trip and a long absence makes this a speculative runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Hamadhan is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 132 lb after a 90-day absence, though he has run over today's going before and his third last time out shows he can find the frame.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose recent form features back-to-back second places at 16f on good ground showing the trip and conditions suit well; a natural hold-up horse placed into the midfield map because the field is stacked with rear-runners, meaning this horse may race slightly out of its natural rhythm and the STYLE_FIT score (0.93) tempers confidence in a typical late finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Arrange has placed three times in that sequence — second two starts back and third last time out — but ranked last on our figures here, she faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 125 lb despite the experience of today's trip and going in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal and Talismans Time are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead over this 1m6f trip at Thirsk, creating a genuinely contested gallop from the outset rather than a false or dawdling pace. With two horses committed to making the running, the pace should be honest and sustained throughout, stretching the field and placing a premium on stamina and relaxed cruising speed rather than a sharp tactical change of gear. This race shape — a competitive, even-tempo gallop on good ground — classically favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce without having to make up excessive ground, rather than true hold-up horses who need a sprint to close. The field also contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Arrange is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield mapping, making a late swooping finish less certain to materialise than the pace shape alone might suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal and Talismans Time trade blows up front and set an honest, even gallop that suits horses travelling just behind them.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace drains the front-runners in the closing stages and hands the advantage to horses who settled prominently and picked up efficiently; Sudu and Mick Collins are both prominent-style performers with form over this type of trip in similar going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters, most likely Sax Appeal, secures an uncontested or lightly-pressed lead and controls tempo on their own terms.
scenarios.body: Sax Appeal has repeatedly placed at 1m6f-plus in good-ground conditions and carries that profile well; if Talismans Time drops away early or is ridden more conservatively, Sax Appeal could dictate a manageable pace and prove hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Sax Appeal and Talismans Time burns genuinely hard and collapses the race wide open in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Pinatique or Hamadhan, both true hold-up types, would need a strongly run race and a clear late run to capitalise; Pinatique is trained by Sir Mark Prescott with a 13-day turnaround suggesting stable confidence, and Hamadhan has placed on good ground at shorter distances.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Denied, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fluctuates, the leaders steal a breather mid-race, and hold-up horses are unable to mount a meaningful challenge from the rear.
scenarios.body: Arrange, despite being mapped to midfield, is a genuine hold-up type racing out of role and would be at a particular disadvantage if the race becomes tactical and positional; a muddling finish would most likely favour whichever prominent runner conserves energy best through the middle portion.

watchPoints.text: Sax Appeal and Talismans Time — watch the early strides carefully to see which horse blinks first and concedes the rail or the lead, as whoever controls the pace from the front will shape the entire tactical outcome.

Arrange — a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion; if this horse cannot drop back to its natural position early, it may race too prominently and burn energy it needs for a late challenge.

Hamadhan — 90 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; watch the paddock and early running for any signs of rustiness, as a horse returning at this distance after a long break carries obvious fitness risk.

Sudu — stepping up notably in trip today (from 12f to 14f is manageable, but context of recent runs at shorter distances is worth noting); if this horse is seen travelling easily in the prominent position through the first mile, it becomes a significant factor late.

Mick Collins — David Nolan is a strong jockey booking for a horse with established staying form; watch whether Nolan positions this horse close enough to the pace early, as a prominent run from the outset is key to this horse's best performances.
